A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SplatFlow and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched across appendix additions, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original Waymo and KITTI reconstruction and novel-view-synthesis results, component ablations, qualitative renderings, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original quantitative evaluations and ablations and adds qualitative dynamic-object decomposition and shifted-trajectory rendering results.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the stated ego-motion procedure: v1 describes compensation on predicted scene flow when constructing the dynamic mask; v2 describes compensating LiDAR inputs before NMFF pretraining and thresholding the resulting motion flow. This is a localized revision to the described procedure; the architecture and training losses are retained.

E1.justification: Waymo and KITTI remain the datasets. V2 adds an off-trajectory rendering scenario on Waymo, evaluating newly generated ego-car trajectories shifted vertically and horizontally from the recorded trajectory (Appendix 10, Figure 12).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding benchmark, training-fraction, runtime, and qualitative comparisons. The new trajectory and decomposition examples evaluate SplatFlow alone; newly cited related work is not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The new trajectory experiment specifies controlled shifts of 0.5 meters upward, downward, leftward, and rightward. Existing benchmark resolutions, metrics, and training-fraction comparisons are retained. V2's identification of the ablation scenes is additional disclosure, and the revised scores do not establish a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: V2 adds qualitative evidence about robustness to trajectory displacement and additional dynamic-object decomposition cases (Figures 11–12). The existing component ablations and KITTI training-data sensitivity analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 retains the same point-estimate and scene-average reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 5 substantially revise all dynamic-only SSIM and LPIPS entries. For example, SplatFlow's Segment 2259 SSIM/LPIPS changes from 0.995/0.016 to 0.899/0.191; the full ablation model changes from 0.984/0.026 to 0.863/0.231. PSNR, whole-scene results, and rankings remain unchanged. Figures 11–12 add qualitative results. The numerical revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: Equation 5 makes the existing bidirectional Chamfer-distance formulation explicit using nearest-neighbor squared distances. This elaborates the existing mathematics; no new theoretical result, assumption, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims: self-supervised dynamic reconstruction through NMFF and Gaussian representations, optical-flow distillation, real-time rendering without tracked 3D boxes, and leading performance on Waymo and KITTI.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the qualitative car comparisons as extreme zooms of distant background vehicles, providing context for interpreting their appearance. Appendix 10 also interprets the new shifted-trajectory examples as demonstrating rendering beyond the recorded ego-car path.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the mid-timestamp reference frame and propagation procedure, clarifies that sky masks are needed only during training, identifies Table 2's scenes as the ablation evaluation set, and adds a project-page pointer for demonstrations. Appendix 6's hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to SuGaR, Instant Neural Graphics Primitives, Behind the Veil, and NeRFusion. It also refines StreetGaussian's description and removes StreetSurf's individual summary while retaining its citation. The central research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording corrections and paragraph revisions, particularly in related work and the NMFF explanation. It adds two short appendix sections and renumbers subsequent material while preserving the main narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: V2 adds decomposition and shifted-trajectory Figures 11–12 and reflows appendix figures and references. Earlier appendix Figures 11–15 largely reappear as Figures 13–17. Existing benchmark tables retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The new qualitative off-trajectory test and decomposition examples modestly strengthen empirical coverage, while clearer initialization details, ablation-scene identification, and demonstration access improve interpretability and reproducibility. However, the substantial dynamic-region SSIM/LPIPS replacements are unexplained, so they do not establish improved numerical reliability. The supported overall gain is limited.
